subject: Literacy
title: Greetings and names
subtopics: My name and my friends’ names
objectives: Children will say or sign a greeting to an adult or friend.
Children will say or point to their own name and a friend’s name.
content: Greeting adults and friends, learning names, and saying please and thank you.
teachingActivities: Greet every child by name each morning; use a wave and a word together; model "Good morning ma" and "Good morning sir" as the school culture requires; praise every attempt.
learnerActivities: Say or sign hello and goodbye, say or point to their own name and a friend’s, and use please and thank you.
assessment: Observe whether each child greets someone, responds to their name and uses please or thank you with support.
expectedOutcomes: Greets someone with a word or wave.
crossCurricular: Personal, Social and Emotional Development: friendship
Understanding the World: me and my family

lessons.title: Hello and goodbye
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will say or wave hello and goodbye.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, make sounds and copy rhythms; many use single words or gestures.
lessons.starter: Wave the puppet and say "Hello, hello!" Wave and say "Goodbye, goodbye!" Ask the children to wave.
teacherActivities: Have the puppet greet each child by name with a wave.
Say "Good morning" and wave. Say "Goodbye" and wave.
Greet the children as a group and ask "Can you say hello?"
Let each child take the puppet and say hello or goodbye to a friend.
learnerActivities: Child waves or says hello back.
Children copy the words and wave.
Children say hello or wave.
Child greets a friend with a wave or a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Have the puppet greet each child by name with a wave. Children: Child waves or says hello back.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Good morning" and wave. Say "Goodbye" and wave. Children: Children copy the words and wave.
Step 3. Teacher: Greet the children as a group and ask "Can you say hello?" Children: Children say hello or wave.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child take the puppet and say hello or goodbye to a friend. Children: Child greets a friend with a wave or a word.

practical.title: Greeting circle
steps: Sit in a circle and pass the puppet.
The child holding the puppet greets the next child.
The next child greets back and passes it on.
practical.safety: Keep the circle wide enough for safe passing. Do not force a shy child to speak; accept a wave or a smile.

differentiation.support: Wave with the child and say hello together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to greet the head teacher or visitor with a word.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we meet someone?
What do we say when we go?

expectedOutcomes: Greets someone with a wave or word
Says goodbye with a wave or word
lessons.conclusion: Say goodbye to the puppet and wave to each other.
lessons.homeConnection: Greet your child with "Good morning" each day and wait for a wave or word.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say or wave hello and goodbye" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Hello, hello, how are you? Hello, hello, I am fine.

lessons.title: My name
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: My name and my friends’ names
objectives: Children will respond to their name and point to their own name card.
successCriteria: Looks or answers when their name is called
Points to their own name card with a photo
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, make sounds and copy rhythms; many use single words or gestures.
lessons.starter: Say "Hello, [child’s name]" and wave. Look at each child and say their name with a smile.
teacherActivities: Hold up each name card and say the name. Ask "Who is this?"
Look in the mirror together and say "I am [name]."
Put three name cards on the mat and ask the child to find theirs.
Say "Hello" to each child by name and wait for a response.
learnerActivities: Children look and say or point to themselves.
Child looks and says or points to their name.
Child points to their card.
Child waves, smiles or says their name.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up each name card and say the name. Ask "Who is this?" Children: Children look and say or point to themselves.
Step 2. Teacher: Look in the mirror together and say "I am [name]." Children: Child looks and says or points to their name.
Step 3. Teacher: Put three name cards on the mat and ask the child to find theirs. Children: Child points to their card.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Hello" to each child by name and wait for a response. Children: Child waves, smiles or says their name.

practical.title: Name cards
steps: Place three name cards on the mat.
Each child finds their own card and holds it up.
The group says the name together.
practical.safety: Keep cards smooth and large so they can be held safely. Handle cards gently and do not tear them.

differentiation.support: Use a photo card and point to the child’s picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend’s name card and say the name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is your name?
questions.expected: Child says or points to their name.

expectedOutcomes: Finds their own name card with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards in the basket and wave goodbye to each name.
lessons.homeConnection: Say your child’s name often and ask them to say it back to you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "respond to their name and point to their own name card" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My friends
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: My name and my friends’ names
objectives: Children will say or point to a friend’s name.
successCriteria: Points to a friend when the name is said
Says a friend’s name with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, make sounds and copy rhythms; many use single words or gestures.
lessons.starter: Roll the ball to a child and say "Hello [name]." Ask the child to roll it back.
teacherActivities: Sit in a circle and roll the ball to a child, naming them. The child rolls it back.
Say a friend’s name and ask "Where is [name]?"
Show a photo card of a friend and ask "Who is this?"
Let each child roll the ball to a friend and say their name.
learnerActivities: Child receives the ball and rolls it on.
Children point to the friend.
Child names or points to the friend.
Child names a friend and rolls the ball.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sit in a circle and roll the ball to a child, naming them. The child rolls it back. Children: Child receives the ball and rolls it on.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a friend’s name and ask "Where is [name]?" Children: Children point to the friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a photo card of a friend and ask "Who is this?" Children: Child names or points to the friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child roll the ball to a friend and say their name. Children: Child names a friend and rolls the ball.

practical.title: Ball and names
steps: Sit in a circle with space between children.
Roll the ball to a friend and say their name.
The friend says hello and rolls it on.
practical.safety: Roll the ball slowly along the floor and keep fingers clear. Sit children with legs apart so they are safe.

differentiation.support: Roll the ball together and say the name with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say a friend’s name and one thing the friend likes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who is this friend?
questions.expected: Child names or points to the friend.

questions.question: Can you say hello to a friend?

expectedOutcomes: Points to a friend by name
Says a friend’s name with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to each friend by name.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about your child’s friends by name and ask them to say hello.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say or point to a friend’s name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Please and thank you
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will use please and thank you when asking for or receiving something.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, make sounds and copy rhythms; many use single words or gestures.
lessons.starter: Hold a toy and say "Please." Give it to the puppet and say "Thank you." Ask "What did I say?"
teacherActivities: Show that when you want a toy you say "Please" and when you get it you say "Thank you".
Hold out a toy and wait for the child to say or sign please.
Give the toy and say "Thank you" and wait.
Pass fruit slices and encourage please and thank you.
learnerActivities: Children watch and repeat the words.
Child says please or makes the sign.
Child says thank you or signs.
Child says please and thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show that when you want a toy you say "Please" and when you get it you say "Thank you". Children: Children watch and repeat the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold out a toy and wait for the child to say or sign please. Children: Child says please or makes the sign.
Step 3. Teacher: Give the toy and say "Thank you" and wait. Children: Child says thank you or signs.
Step 4. Teacher: Pass fruit slices and encourage please and thank you. Children: Child says please and thank you.

practical.title: Toy shop
steps: Set up a toy shop with a basket of toys.
Each child asks for a toy with please.
They say thank you when they get it.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before giving any food and use only washed fruit. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Use a sign for please and say it with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the shopkeeper and give toys to friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we ask?
What do we say when we get something?

lessons.homeConnection: Model please and thank you at mealtimes and wait for your child to say them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use please and thank you when asking for or receiving something" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 greetings check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child greets others and responds to their name.
successCriteria: Greets someone with a word or wave
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, make sounds and copy rhythms; many use single words or gestures.
lessons.starter: Sing the hello song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: hello puppet, name cards and toy shop.
At each station greet the child and wait for a response. Ask "What is your name?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child greets, responds or points.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: hello puppet, name cards and toy shop. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station greet the child and wait for a response. Ask "What is your name?" Children: Child greets, responds or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Greeting stations
practical.safety: Use soft toys and large cards. Supervise each station and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and accept gestures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to greet a visitor.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: greets with a word or wave; responds to their own name; says or signs please and thank you.

questions.question: What do you say when you meet someone?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Greets with a word or wave
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and wave to everyone.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise hello, goodbye, please and thank you at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child greets others and responds to their name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
